name: promote_types
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::promote_types(ScalarType type1, ScalarType type2) -> ScalarType. Registered schemas: aten::promote_types(ScalarType type1, ScalarType type2) -> ScalarType. Original Gems pytest (tests/test_promote_types.py) owns the full contract: it selects and checks the accepted dtype pairs across the promotion lattice, integer ScalarType-code arguments, zero-dim integer-tensor arguments, the rejected/unpromotable pairs (Float8 mixed with anything other than itself; uint16/uint32/uint64 paired with any non-floating dtype other than an identical dtype, i.e. bool, integer, another wide-uint, complex or Float8), non-ScalarType argument errors and the exact return type; selection is by family split and native ATen is the oracle for both the returned ScalarType code and the rejected set. Do not narrow, delete or adapt those tests to this single signature. Semantics: a host-side dtype query with no tensor result; it computes the promoted result dtype of two ScalarType operands and returns a Python int ScalarType code (the tests assert type(res_out) is int and equality with torch.ops.aten.promote_types). type1/type2 accept torch.dtype values, raw int enum codes (e.g. uint8=0, int8=1, int32=3, int64=4, float16=5, float32=6, bool=11, bfloat16=15, uint16=27) or zero-dim integer tensors holding a code. Invalid operands (str, None, float, list, tuple, or mixed Float8/wide-uint pairs) raise a standard Python error (TypeError/ValueError/RuntimeError). This definition models the representative overload only; conditional, overload-dependent and error behavior remain expressed solely by the original pytest.
